claim_text: A cyber incident at one of Next's suppliers gave outsiders access to certain Next data
summary: In a notice to the London Stock Exchange on Nov 23, 2026, Next said a third-party online supplier had a cyber incident that led to unauthorised access to certain 'benign' data relating to Next.
detail: This is Next's own notice, also listed on its investor page. It is a supplier's systems that were accessed, not, Next says, Next's own. BBC News, The Guardian, Reuters, The Register and City AM all repeat the same statement, so they add no separate confirmation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company itself told the stock exchange that outsiders accessed its data at a supplier.
notes: Company admission, Tier 1. Says a supplier was breached; does not say Next was breached directly.

claim_text: Next says its own systems were not compromised
summary: The notice says Next is confident its own systems have not been compromised and that this is an incident affecting the supplier's environment.
detail: This is Next's own assessment, and its investigation is still ongoing. No outside party has checked it. Reuters, City AM and The Register repeat it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Only the company says so; nothing independent confirms or contradicts it.
notes: Company's own claim, relayed by outlets. Counted as one source.

claim_text: Whether customer personal data was taken
summary: Next says current evidence indicates no customer personal data has been compromised.
detail: Next's wording is 'current evidence', and its investigation is ongoing. City AM's headline and first line say hackers accessed some customers' data, but its own later paragraphs repeat Next saying customer data was not affected; we treat that as a loose summary, not a separate claim. Nothing shows customer data was taken, and nothing rules it out yet.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company says there is no evidence; no outside source shows otherwise.
notes: Absence of evidence so far. Revisit on any ICO, Next or supplier update.

claim_text: Next calls the data 'benign' and says it cannot be used for fraud
summary: Next says the data is limited and, on its current assessment, cannot be used for fraud. The Guardian says it is understood to exclude contact details, addresses, passwords and bank details.
detail: The 'benign' label and the fraud assessment are Next's own. The Guardian's detail is unattributed ('it is understood'). The Register notes Next would not say what was accessed or how much.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company describes the data; no outside source has seen it.

summary: Next has not named the supplier. It describes it only as 'one of our third-party online suppliers'. The Guardian calls it a technology supplier.
detail: The Register says Next declined to name the supplier when asked. We found no supplier statement.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company has not said, and we found no other source that names it.
notes: Do not guess a name from outside commentary.

claim_text: Who was behind the incident, and how they got in
summary: Neither Next nor any outlet we read says who carried out the incident or how they got into the supplier. The Register says Next would not say what was accessed or how much.
detail: The Guardian and City AM call the intruders 'hackers', but no source identifies a group, a method or a motive. No ransom claim or leak-site claim was found; we did not look at any such sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing in the notice or the coverage says how it happened or who did it.

claim_text: Next says it is working with the supplier, law enforcement and regulators
summary: Next says it is working closely with the supplier, law enforcement and relevant regulatory authorities, and is treating the matter with the utmost seriousness.
detail: Next does not name the regulator. We found no statement from the UK data protection regulator (the ICO) and none from police.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company says so in its notice; no agency has confirmed it.
